metadata.title: Davis Allen - Catches just one pass in Week 2
metadata.description: Allen caught his only target for seven yards in Monday night's win over the Giants.
metadata.analysis: The tight end played 52 percent of the offensive snaps, trailing both Colby Parkinson and Terrance Ferguson at the position on a night the Rams again used a heavy dose of tight ends with Puka Nacua (hip) inactive. Allen would need an injury ahead of him to enter the conversation for fantasy.

metadata.title: Davis Allen - Finishes game in Melbourne
metadata.description: Allen (head) returned to the Week 1 contest against the 49ers, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Allen exited early in the contest with a potential concussion. The tight end's confirmed return to the Week 1 contest in Australia means an independent neurologist deemed that he did not have a concussion and was all set to play. Allen should be ready to practice throughout Week 2 and suit up for Monday's game against the Giants.

metadata.title: Davis Allen - Getting examined for possible concussion
metadata.description: Allen is getting examined for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Thursday's matchup with the 49ers.
metadata.analysis: The tight end recorded one catch on one target for 13 yards before exiting. The Rams use as many as four tight ends, and in Allen's absence, Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee and Terrance Ferguson are the players still available at the position.

metadata.title: Davis Allen Enters Concussion Protocol After Thursday's Loss
metadata.description: Los Angeles Rams tight end Davis Allen (concussion) was evaluated for a concussion during Thursday's Week 1 loss against the San Francisco 49ers. Allen officially entered concussion protocol and was listed as questionable to return, but he didn't get back into the game. He suffered the injury after taking a brutal hit near the sideline. Upon standing up, Allen appeared disoriented and had trouble staying on his feet. He left the playing field and ended up being carted to the locker room, finishing the game with one catch for 13 yards. Allen led the tight end room in total yards, and Tyler Higbee was the only tight end with multiple catches. (He had two.) The Rams have 11 days until their next game, making it difficult to say whether Allen will clear concussion protocol in time for Week 2. The tight end room should be able to survive his injury with a three-headed unit of Terrance Ferguson, Colby Parkinson, and Higbee.

metadata.title: Davis Allen - Good to go for Week 1
metadata.description: Allen (quadriceps) is not listed on the Rams' injury report ahead of Thursday's game against the 49ers, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Allen missed a few weeks of action during training camp with the injury but is all good for the opener. The tight end appeared in all 17 regular-season games last season, finishing with career highs in targets (33), catches (24), yards (208) and touchdowns (three) on 52 percent of the Rams' offensive snaps. He's expected to again be part of Los Angeles' heavy tight end usage this season.

metadata.title: Davis Allen - Logs limited practice Monday
metadata.description: Allen (quadriceps) was a limited participant in Monday's training camp practice, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Allen has been limited to side work in training camp while recovering from a quadriceps injury, but his ability to practice Monday, even in a limited capacity, is a positive sign for the 2023 fifth-rounder. He's unlikely to play in Thursday's preseason finale against the Chargers, but Allen is working his way toward being available for the Rams' regular-season opener against the 49ers on Thursday, Sept. 10.

metadata.title: Davis Allen Expected to Return "Within the Next Week"
metadata.description: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay said that tight end Davis Allen (quadriceps) is expected to return to practice "within the next week," per Stu Jackson of therams.com. Jackson also reports that Allen is expected to be ready for Week 1. Across 17 games with Los Angeles in 2025, Allen recorded 24 catches for 208 yards and three touchdowns on 33 targets. While he's unlikely to provide fantasy-relevant production himself, Allen's presence further complicates the Rams' crowded tight end room for fantasy managers. In addition to Allen, Los Angeles has veterans Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee, 2025 second-round pick Terrance Ferguson, and 2026 second-round pick Max Klare as other tight ends on its roster. While the Rams use multiple tight end personnel groupings at one of the highest rates in the league, their depth at the position makes it hard for fantasy managers to rely on any one tight end in Los Angeles for consistent production.

metadata.title: Davis Allen - Nearing return to practice
metadata.description: Coach Sean McVay noted Tuesday that Allen (quad) is expected to return to practice "within the next week," Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: McVay added that Allen -- who is dealing with a quad issue -- is expected be ready for Week 1 action against the 49ers, barring any unforeseen setbacks. During the 2025 regular season, Davis recorded 33 targets for 24 catches, 208 yards and three touchdowns over 17 games. However, as the coming campaign approaches, his path to volume is murky, with all of Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson and Max Klare also in the Rams' TE mix.

metadata.title: Davis Allen dealing with quad injury
metadata.description: Rams coach Sean McVay said TE TE Davis Allen is dealing with a quad.
metadata.analysis: McVay said they will give Allen "some time" before he returns to practice. "Davis is going to be a big part of what we do," McVay said. He won't be on the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Davis Allen - Taking reserved approach to injury
metadata.description: The Rams are giving Allen (quadriceps) "some time" before he returns to practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Coach Sean McVay said that due to the soft-tissue nature of the injury, they do not want to rush Allen back. The tight end was a prominent part of the Rams' 13-personnel offense during the 2025 season, drawing 33 targets for 24 receptions, 208 yards and three touchdowns over 17 regular-season games. The 25-year-old was also a prominent member of the trenches in the McVay scheme, logging additional offensive and special teams snaps that helped lead the team to its 12-5 record. Now in a contract year, when Allen does return, he is set to become a consistent contributor for the 2026 Rams.
